## post by Roman_Ahmmed on Jan 4
Vila Franca de Xira is a city and municipality located in the Lisbon District of Portugal. It is situated on both banks of the Tagus River, approximately 32 km northeast of the Portuguese capital, Lisbon.
During the COVID-19 pandemic, on June 23, 2020, I visited Vila Franca de Xira for the first time. Since then, I have frequently returned, especially in the late afternoon, to enjoy its beauty.
The mural features António Alves Redol (1911–1969), an influential Portuguese writer and a key figure in the neo-realist literary movement in Portugal. Born in Vila Franca de Xira, his legacy is celebrated throughout the country for his significant impact on the cultural landscape of the 20th century.
You can find this type of mural in various parts of Portugal. The purpose of these murals is to showcase Portuguese culture and highlight prominent figures in the country’s history.
I really enjoy train journeys, and I have to take the train to reach my workplace along this route. It was during these travels that I discovered this place.
Sometimes, **I see local Portuguese people fishing with spears, which inspired me to get my own fishing license. I tried fishing a couple of times**, but I no longer come here due to my busy schedule.
**The best way to get from Lisbon to Vila Franca de Xira (Station)**.
Comboios de Portugal operates a train from Lisbon, Oriente Train Station to Vila Franca de Xira Train Station every 20 minutes. Tickets cost €2–14, and the journey takes 18 minutes.

# What to see and do in Vila Franca de Xira
## Information
**Vila Franca de Xira** is a municipality in the district of Lisbon, made up of several parishes -the homonymous one is the seat-, bathed by the Tagus river and a stop on the Portuguese Way within the capital's metropolitan area. Among its highlights: the Tagus Estuary Park walking trail; the municipal market, with its beautiful tiled building; and the municipal museum, housed in an 18th-century building that preserves the memory of the territory.
This territory refers the first data of foundation and origin to the archaeological sites around Lisbon. From the studies carried out in the area, we know that its first settlements date back to prehistoric times, with the presence of Lusitanian tribes. Throughout its history, it has been a territory occupied by Romans and Arabs, until its conquest in the Middle Ages by the Christian kingdoms of the north of the peninsula.

# What to see and do in Vila Franca de Xira
## What to see in Vila Franca de Xira
### Tagus Estuary Park
There is a **pedestrian path** that runs along the Tagus River. It is a perfect walk to enjoy the tranquility and the beautiful riverside scenery.

# What to see and do in Vila Franca de Xira
## What to see in Vila Franca de Xira
### Municipal market
Something very remarkable of Portugal, are its **traditional tiled buildings**, which endure with the passage of time and are an identifying element and of great value of the Portuguese culture. In the municipal market, you can enjoy its beautiful tiled construction and ornamented with traditional Portuguese paintings. In addition, there you can find a great variety of typical products of the gastronomy of the area.

# What to see and do in Vila Franca de Xira
## What to see in Vila Franca de Xira
### Municipal Museum of Vila Franca de Xira
Located in a building dating back to the 18th century, the museum aims to preserve, protect and disseminate the memory of the territory of **Vila Franca de Xira**.

# What to see and do in Vila Franca de Xira
## What to see in Vila Franca de Xira
### Museum of Neo-Realism
It has been located in its current building, designed by the architect Alcino Soutinho, since 2007. The museum is currently seeking to broaden its foundational horizons and expand its outreach to other contemporary artistic styles. www.cm-vfxira.pt
